## Welcome

Benedikt Gräler completed his Diploma in Mathematics in 2009 and earned his PhD in Geoinformatics in 2014. He conducted his research at the [Institute for Geoinformatics](https://www.uni-muenster.de/Geoinformatics/) in the field of spatial statistics; his developments and findings are collected in his dissertation [*Developing Spatio-Temporal Copulas*](files/publications/Diss_Benedikt_Graeler.pdf).

In January 2016, he joined the [Institute of Hydrology, Water Resources Management and Environmental Engineering](http://www.hydrology.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/index.html.en) at Ruhr-University Bochum as a research associate and contributed to the SFB 823 "[Statistical modelling of nonlinear dynamic processes](https://www.statistik.tu-dortmund.de/sfb823.html)". Since May 2017, he has worked at [52°North Spatial Information Research GmbH](https://52north.org) as a research associate and consultant leading the Spatio-Temporal Data Science Lab. In May 2021, Benedikt became one of the managing directors of 52°North. He is responsible for the research pursued at 52°North and keeps close contact with universities and associated research partners. Together with [con terra](https://www.conterra.de) and the [University of Münster](https://www.uni-muenster.de), he initiated the [Spatial AI Nexus Münster](https://www.spatial-ai-nexus.ms), a transfer network that brings applied spatial AI research into practice for public authorities, companies and international organisations.

Beyond 52°North, Benedikt serves as Vice-President of [EUROGI](https://eurogi.org), the European umbrella organisation for geographic information, and as Europe delegate of the [Deutscher Dachverband für Geoinformation (DDGI)](https://ddgi.de).

## Research

At 52°North, Benedikt researches Information Systems for spatial and spatio-temporal data integrating statistical methods. Benedikt's focus in mathematical research has been on copulas and he extended the concept to the spatial and spatio-temporal domain. This includes modelling spatio-temporal random fields, trajectory data of various kinds, as well as identifying and modelling extreme events in space and time. Please take a look at his [publications](publications.qmd) for a detailed list of recent professional activities. With the help of [shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/), he made different copula families interactively accessible in his [copulatheque](https://copulatheque.shinyapps.io/copulas/).

## Software

In parallel to his research, Benedikt develops the R package [sfcopula](https://github.com/BenGraeler/sfcopula), which models spatial and spatio-temporal random fields with vine copulas. It is the successor of [spcopula](https://github.com/BenGraeler/spcopula) and builds on [sf](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) and [stars](https://r-spatial.github.io/stars/) instead of the former sp and spacetime packages. Besides his own packages, he contributes to a set of further R packages related to copulas as well as spatial and spatio-temporal data representation and analysis, such as [gstat](https://github.com/r-spatial/gstat), [spacetime](https://github.com/edzer/spacetime), [VineCopula](https://github.com/tnagler/VineCopula) and [trajectories](https://github.com/edzer/trajectories). A detailed overview can be found on his [GitHub](https://github.com/BenGraeler) profile.
